title: Cross-asset time-series momentum
hypothesis: Trend across ~23 liquid ETFs earns a positive, crisis-positive premium.
question: Does a simple multi-horizon trend rule on liquid ETFs across equities, rates, credit, commodities and FX earn a positive return that holds up in crises?
prior: Time-series momentum is documented across asset classes over a century (Moskowitz, Ooi and Pedersen 2012; Hurst, Ooi and Pedersen 2017), and it tends to pay in prolonged sell-offs.
citations: Moskowitz, T., Ooi, Y. H. & Pedersen, L. H. (2012). Time Series Momentum. JFE 104(2).
Hurst, B., Ooi, Y. H. & Pedersen, L. H. (2017). A Century of Evidence on Trend-Following Investing. JPM 44(1).
method: Signal = average sign of 3-, 6- and 12-month returns; inverse-vol sizing to 15% per asset; gross capped at 3×.
Monthly rebalance, weights lagged one day, 7 bps on turnover. Rules-based, so the whole history is out-of-sample.
Robustness on 5 perturbations (horizons, vol target, long-or-flat).
verdict_reason: Sharpe 0.67 with near-zero correlation to SPY, and it beat SPY in 4 of 5 crisis windows (GFC +7.1% vs SPY −43.4%), though it lost money in two of them. Cleared the bar to build a carry sleeve and blend.
lessons: Diversification across asset classes is the free lunch that daily data can deliver.
footer: Research code is private; methods summarised below.
